title: Writing Style Matters: An Examination of Bias and Fairness in Information Retrieval Systems

bias_targets.methodology: Rewriting queries and documents into nine distinct communication styles (e.g., formal, informal with emojis, emotive, simple) using an LLM, ranking the documents by text embedding cosine similarity, and calculating an unfairness score based on the spread and standard deviation of their average rankings.

Comparing the correctness evaluation scores of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems by measuring the semantic text embedding similarity between ground-truth answers and diverse responses generated by different LLMs (e.g., FlanT5, Llama2) to see if metrics unfairly favor specific generation styles like verbosity or conciseness.
